question: Which Indian state passed the Right to Health (RTH) bill, which guarantees access to equitable healthcare services for all patients in March 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajasthan** became the first state in India to pass the **Right to Health (RTH)** bill in March 2023.
 
• The bill guarantees access to **equitable healthcare services** for all patients.
 
• The act mandates that both **private and public healthcare institutions** provide necessary medical services without delay.
 
• It aims to ensure that **no patient is denied medical treatment** due to lack of funds.
 
• The bill includes provisions for **free emergency treatment** in both private and public hospitals.
 
• Patients have the right to receive **information** about their medical condition and treatment options.
 
• A **grievance redressal mechanism** is established to address complaints related to healthcare services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu**__

 __
 
• Tamil Nadu is known for its **advanced healthcare infrastructure** and medical tourism.
 
• The state has several **well-established government and private hospitals**.
 
• It is home to the **Chennai Medical College**, one of the oldest medical colleges in India.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**__
 __
 
• Gujarat has made significant strides in **public health** and is known for its **healthcare schemes**.
 
• It has implemented various **public health programs** to improve maternal and child health.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**__
 
 
• Maharashtra has a mix of **urban and rural healthcare facilities**.
 
• The state is home to some of the top medical institutions like the **Tata Memorial Hospital** for cancer treatment.
